title: Weekly Focus Scrapbook — Sprint Micro-OKRs & Habit Tests
body:
Context:
This is a messy weekly scratchbook where I try to stitch together micro-OKRs, habit experiments, and quick metrics that actually move the needle for my work (and sanity). Not a polished plan — more a living log of tests, calls, and tiny wins.

Top intent for the week: keep at least 3 high-focus blocks (~90 minutes each) and convert one recurring meeting into async notes. Try a 10-minute end-of-day micro-retro every workday.

Micro-OKRs (Sprint = 7 days)
- Objective A: Reduce context switch cost so deep work becomes predictable.
  - Key result A1: 3x focus blocks completed (90m min) in the week.
  - Key result A2: < 2 meetings scheduled during my deep slots.
  - Quick signal: Count of interruptions (Slack pings that required >5 min follow-up).
- Objective B: Improve prompt evaluation throughput for the playground project.
  - Key result B1: Run 20 short prompt evals (<=5 prompts each).
  - Key result B2: Land 2 clear examples to add to the eval suite.

Habit tests (small, 3-day experiments)
- 10-min EOD micro-retro: log 3 things (what worked, what didn't, one pivot).
- No-meetings-before-11am: see if first deep block becomes consistent.
- Pomodoro-ish variant: 50/10 for focus blocks (try for 3 blocks).

Streak ledger (manual count)
- Day 1 (Mon): deep block x2, evals x6, retro yes. Notes: unexpected paging bug slowed evals.
- Day 2 (Tue): deep block x1, meeting replaced with async doc — huge win.
- Day 3 (Wed): deep block x3, evals x8, retro yes. Observed: shorter evals with clear hypothesis perform better.

Quick metrics snapshot (manual, daily)
- Focus blocks completed: [2,1,3,null,null,null,null]
- Prompt evals completed: [6,4,8,null,null,null,null]
- Interruptions logged (>5m): [3,5,1,null,null,null,null]

Decisions & small actions to take
- Convert Tuesday recurring sync with infra to an async summary; propose a 2-week trial. (Assigned to: myself; due: Thu)
- Create a tiny eval template: hypothesis + input set (5 examples) + pass/fail + note. Ship to playground repo. (Link in linked_artifacts)
- If interruptions >3 on any day, do a 15-min triage at EOD to categorize and add rules (mute, auto-reply, schedule).

Open questions / Thoughts to capture
- Is "focus blocks" the right unit? Maybe track "uninterrupted minutes" instead — more granular but heavier to log.
- What counts as a meaningful prompt eval? Right now I conflate quality checks with throughput; need a binary pass/fail anchor.
- Could handoff to a weekly async digest be a scalable way to reduce meeting count across the team? Pilot with one recurring meeting first.

Micro-retro (fast synthesis after day 3)
- Wins: Replacing one meeting with async notes freed a 90-minute slot — big momentum. The EOD retro sharpens prioritization (only 1-2 pivots per day now).
- Frictions: Logging metrics manually is a pain — consider a tiny Google Sheet with checkboxes and one formula for sums.
- Hypothesis for next week: If I protect two morning deep slots for four days and force async for 2 recurring syncs, my prompt eval throughput will increase by 30%.

Next week experiments (planned)
- Automate the ledger: simple sheet + daily reminder; aim to reduce logging time to <2 minutes.
- Introduce a simple pass/fail rubric for prompt evals and record time-to-first-result.
- Invite Mikael to run a paired deep block session once to observe context-switch triggers.

Notes to self (fragmented raw lines)
- Try "focus-once" Slack status before deep block.
- If interrupted: log and defer reply by default; add quick template for "snooze" responses.
- Keep evals short: 5 inputs max until hypothesis validated.
- Celebrate small wins: 1-line win channel in personal notes.

Anchors for longer-term (not for this week)
- Build a micro-dashboard showing weekly streaks and interruption trends.
- Make a 1-pager on async meeting trials and template for replacements.

References / links
- Quick eval template (placeholder): github.com/redwood-inference/personal-evals/template.md
- Meeting async example: confluence://playbooks/async-sync-template

End.
